newsitem.title: USA: 'Beavis and Butt-head' rule at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: 'Beavis and Butt-head' rule at U.S. box office.

text.p: Two socially stunted cartoon characters ruled at the box office this weekend as "Beavis and Butt-head Do America" opened in the No. 1 position with $20.5 million, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

The tally is the highest ever for a December opening, and the animated movie left last week's No. 1, "Jerry Maguire," in a distant second at $13.4 million. "101 Dalmatians" held steady in third with $6.8 million.
"Beavis and Butt-head Do America" marks the feature debut of MTV's wisecracking 14-year-old boys, whose favorite pursuit is to watch heavy metal bands on TV and employ sexual innuendo.

Directed by the pair's creator, Mike Judge, the movie takes the pair on a cross-country tour during which they unwittingly become caught up in a terrorist incident. The movie is released by Paramount Pictures which, along with MTV, is owned by Viacom Inc.. The movie averaged a stunning $9,361 from 2,190 screens.

"Jerry Maguire," a romantic comedy starring Tom Cruise as a sports agent, dropped 22 percent from last weekend and has a 10-day total of $36.6 million. The movie, which is released by TriStar Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp., averaged $5,294 per screen.
Walt Disney Co.'s "101 Dalmatians" fell by 24 percent from last weekend, and averaged $2,344 per screen. After 26 days in release, it has earned $84.6 million.

Two new releases battled for fourth and fifth. Officially, the horror movie "Scream" grossed $6.6 million followed by the George Clooney/Michelle Pfeiffer romantic comedy "One Fine Day" with $6.1 million. However, some movie industry people said "Scream's" estimate was too optimistic and its tally is probably closer to $5.7 million, which would make it fifth.

"Scream" is directed by Wes Craven and features an ensemble cast including Neve Campbell, Drew Barrymore and Courteney Cox. It is distributed by Disney-owned Miramax Films. It averaged a decent $4,459 from 1,413 screens.
"One Fine Day" is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp.. It averaged about $3,116 from 1,945 theaters.

The other wide release to open this weekend was the James Garner/Jack Lemmon presidential comedy "My Fellow Americans." It took the ninth spot with a weak $2.8 million and $1,462 per-screen average. The movie is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc..
